metadata.ablationNote: Enhanced baseline at N=16, generated with the same baseline prompt as the N=16 count-matched harness PLUS an explicit category-diversity instruction (at least one accessibility test, one persistence test, one internationalization test, one error-handling test). Tests the hypothesis that an informed practitioner could close the category-coverage gap by hand-coding the categories the enrichment stage discovers automatically.

testCases.title: Add a new todo via Enter key
Input field clears after successful submission
Mark an active todo as complete
Unmark a completed todo back to active
Delete a todo via the destroy button
Filter list to show only active todos
Filter list to show only completed todos
All filter restores full list after a sub-filter is active
Clear completed removes only completed todos
Items-left count reflects only uncompleted todos
Footer is hidden when the todo list is empty
'Clear completed' button is absent when no todos are completed
Submitting empty or whitespace-only input adds no todo
Destroy button is only visible on hover, not by default
Filter buttons and destroy button are keyboard accessible
Todo state persists across a browser page refresh

grades.reason: The test case is fully specified with clear preconditions, observable steps, and a precise multi-part expected outcome that directly matches the design's described behavior for todo creation, footer visibility, item count, and default filter state.
This is a standard, observable happy-path check for a well-known TodoMVC behavior that any production implementation must satisfy.
The test case is fully specified with clear preconditions, observable steps, and three distinct verifiable expected outcomes that directly map to documented design components.

The test case covers a well-defined, fully observable toggle interaction that the design's checkbox component implicitly supports, with clear preconditions, unambiguous steps, and verifiable expected outcomes including UI state and counter update.

The test case correctly exercises the destroy button's hover-visibility behavior and verifies the footer disappears when the last todo is deleted, both of which are explicitly specified in the design.
The test fully exercises the Active filter with correct preconditions, observable expected outcomes covering list state, filter highlight, and count accuracy, all consistent with the design.
The test case has clear preconditions, unambiguous steps, and a fully observable expected outcome that directly exercises the Completed filter described in the design.
The test directly exercises the filter switching behavior described in the design and verifies both the list content and the visual state of the selected filter button.
The test case is fully specified with concrete preconditions, unambiguous steps, and verifiable expected outcomes that cover all observable side effects of the clear-completed action.
The test directly verifies the design's 'N items left' counter behavior with a clear, reproducible precondition, unambiguous steps, and a precisely observable expected outcome.

The test directly verifies the design's explicit rule that the footer is only visible when at least one todo exists, and uses a concrete, observable precondition and action to reach the empty-list state.

The test directly verifies the design's explicit visibility rule that 'Clear completed' appears only when at least one completed todo exists, with clear preconditions and an observable expected outcome.

Preventing empty/whitespace todo creation is a universally expected implicit behavior for this category of application, the steps are unambiguous and reproducible, and the expected outcome is fully observable.
The test directly verifies the destroy button's hover-only visibility behavior, which is explicitly specified in the design, with clear preconditions and an observable expected outcome.

Keyboard accessibility for filter buttons and destroy buttons is a standard production requirement for any web application, the preconditions are concrete and sufficient, and each step has a clear observable expected outcome.

Persistence across page reload is a standard implicit requirement for any production todo application, the preconditions and steps are clear and reproducible, and the expected outcome is fully observable and specific.
